object_description: two very compact solitary volumes of the same typological family set in a landscaped area
geometry_property: denser and less open research volume
design_condition: the two buildings continue the principle of solitary volumes set in a landscaped expanse, with the landscape treated as the central actor of the perception of the place

positive: The phenomenological interpretation of the place and the landscape is not uninteresting
The two buildings are from the same typological family, effective in their distributive rationality
The teaching building benefits from a slight over-sizing of the corridors on the upper floors
This suggests a possible appropriation of these spaces beyond strict functionality
The perspectives they open on the distant landscape agree with the authors discourse
Meeting spaces in the north seek to restore welcome breathing space
The emphasis on the spatial qualities of the ground floors is welcome
The cafeteria and the large auditorium are identified as the two major moments of student living together
The project is attentive to developing meeting spaces and informal exchanges, which the jury praises
Despite excess floor areas and large slab spans the construction is economical
The cost of the work falls within the average range
negative: The interpretation cannot avoid territorial and not only landscape reflection
Whether the solitary-in-landscape principle is still relevant given densification is questioned
The jury could not agree unanimously with the authors implicit affirmative answer
The perspective views forget the presence of some university constructions in the field of vision
The research building is spatially more compact, denser and less open to the outside
It plays on the qualities of its counterpart only in a minor way
Meeting spaces are surrounded by lifts, toilets and technical rooms
The distribution of practical work over too many floors is problematic
Access to the basement for the animal room is impossible
Flows linked to research labs are unresolved
The option of two very compact volumes appears outdated
Compactness without patio or atrium comes at the expense of natural lighting
Shadows projected on the neighbouring terrace are to be feared
The ground floor transition slab requires significant load absorption and large overhangs
Its thickness is minimised and prestressing is surely necessary
The spans in the eastern building are not reasonable and require significant slab thicknesses
